meta.note: Hand-written briefs for the Khemet / alchemy / chemistry run. Leads, not evidence.

asks: What chemical technologies is ancient Egypt (Kemet, Khemet) securely documented to have practised, from analysis of objects and texts: pigments (Egyptian blue, Egyptian green, frit), glass and faience, metallurgy (copper, gold, bronze), mummification materials (natron, resins, oils), cosmetics (galena, lead compounds, kohl), dyes, fermentation, medical recipes? Give dates and the kind of evidence (chemical analysis, texts, workshop remains).
Which of these are measured by archaeometry versus only described in texts?

ancient Egyptian glass faience production workshop Qantir
Egyptian cosmetics lead compounds laurionite Walter 1999 Nature

asks: What is the evidence and scholarly status of the claim that the word 'chemistry'/'alchemy' derives from Kemet/Khem/'black land' (Egyptian kmt)? What are the competing etymologies (Greek chyma/cheo, Arabic kimiya, others) and who argues which? State clearly which is most widely accepted and why.
What do the earliest attestations of the words chemeia / chymeia say (e.g. Zosimus, Suda, Plutarch's Isis and Osiris use of Chemia for Egypt)?

Plutarch Isis and Osiris Chemia Egypt
alchemy etymology al-kimiya Arabic Greek origin dispute

asks: What textual and material evidence shows alchemy / early chemistry in Greco-Roman Egypt (Alexandria, Panopolis): Leiden papyrus X, Stockholm papyrus, Pseudo-Democritus Physika kai Mystika, Zosimus of Panopolis, Mary the Jewess (Maria Prophetissa) and her apparatus, Cleopatra the Alchemist? Dates, languages, and what they actually describe (practical dye/metal recipes versus theory).
Is there any evidence for alchemy in pharaonic Egypt before the Ptolemies? State what is absent as well as what is present.

Zosimus of Panopolis alchemy texts dating

asks: How did Greco-Egyptian alchemy reach modern chemistry: Byzantine collections, Arabic translation and Jabirian / Rhazes work, Latin translations (e.g. Robert of Chester 1144), medieval and early-modern European alchemy, Boyle, Newton, Lavoisier? Which links are documented in texts and manuscripts?

What does the historiography say (Newman and Principe on 'chymistry', Principe's work) about whether alchemy and chemistry were separate? And what do sceptics say about popular claims that modern chemistry is simply 'Egyptian science', or that Hermes Trismegistus / the Emerald Tablet are pharaonic-era (the Hermetica and Tabula Smaragdina are generally dated to Roman Egypt and Arabic sources respectively; check)?
